title: PrettyChat — cross-addon globals, settings validation, savedvars and comments
cluster_summary: Every finding in this cluster is real. The only serious one is PC-R-01. LootHistory compiles the loot, currency and roll-won patterns from the chat globals once and never rebuilds them, but PrettyChat rewrites those globals in the middle of a session, so LootHistory stops recording loot until the next /reload. The fix belongs in LootHistory/core/Util.lua as a cache keyed on the source strings, and PrettyChat needs no code change. The PrettyChat items are small local fixes: refuse a blank format (PC-R-02), skip pruning when the stored stamp is newer than this build (PC-R-04), correct the false taint sentence (PC-R-05) and correct the wrong figures in comments (PC-R-06). PC-R-13 does not need fixing.

verdicts.assessment: Verified in LootHistory/core/Util.lua. Line 152 (lootPatterns or Build...) and line 215 (currencyPatterns) build their patterns once, and lines 170-179 cache rollWonPattern, including a cached false when the global is absent. PrettyChat rewrites those globals on settings writes, profile changes, enable and disable, and at combat boundaries, so self-loot and currency records are silently lost until /reload.
verdicts.remediation: In LootHistory core/Util.lua, store each global's source string beside its compiled pattern. On every parse, compare the stored string with the current _G value and rebuild when it differs. Apply this to loot, currency and RollWonPattern, and do not leave a cached false in place when the global changes. Add a LootHistory test that swaps _G.LOOT_ITEM_SELF in the middle of a session. Open a LootHistory issue that cites PrettyChat handoff H-1, and track the work under a LootHistory id. PrettyChat needs no code change. Only refresh the stale Util.lua line citations in PrettyChat docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:202.

verdicts.assessment: The panel path is real. Panel.lua sends "" to Schema.Set, the conversion-signature prefix check accepts it, and the empty string is stored and written into the Blizzard global, so that message type prints blank. The CLI already refuses a blank value. A player can easily hit this, and the fix is cheap.
verdicts.remediation: In Schema refusedBySignature (or the row set), refuse an empty or whitespace-only format and return a localized message from a new enUS key. Add test_schema cases for "" and "   ", and regenerate docs/test-cases.md and the README badge in the same commit.

verdicts.assessment: Verified in Database.lua RunMigrations. A stamp that is ahead of SCHEMA_VERSION is normalized down, and PruneOrphans always runs, so a rollback permanently deletes the overrides a newer build stored. Only a rollback can trigger this, which is why the severity is lowered to low, but the data loss is silent and permanent and the fix is one early return.
verdicts.remediation: In RunMigrations, when the stored schemaVersion is greater than SCHEMA_VERSION, write a debug log and return without pruning or restamping. Deliberately update test_database.lua:61-65, add a case that shows overrides survive a stamp of 99, and update the RunMigrations header comment.

verdicts.assessment: docs/data-flow.md:141 literally says "`_G` writes don't taint", which is false. The claim that actually holds is that only non-protected chat formatting reads those globals. Correcting the docs costs nothing and stops future combat-guard decisions from resting on a wrong premise.
verdicts.remediation: Rewrite that sentence. It should say that the writes do taint the overridden globals, but only non-protected chat formatting reads them, so no protected path is affected. Optionally add an owner in-client smoke note (issecurevariable check). It is not a gate.

verdicts.assessment: The comments contradict each other on the report length ('500+', '500-line' and 'eighty-odd'), and Schema.lua says 'nine addons' when the roster has eleven. This has no runtime impact, but it misleads readers. Comment volume on its own is not a defect.
verdicts.remediation: Fix only the wrong figures. Describe the Test() report size without an exact count (or recount it from real Test() output), and reword Schema.lua:104-105 so it gives no addon count. No wholesale trimming of comments.

verdicts.assessment: The "1.6.0" fallback in Namespace.lua:8 is used only when NS.Meta returns nil, which never happens in the client. It agrees with the TOC today, and bump-version already updates code constants. A pinning test would only add churn to every version bump.
